title: Zuriel Hebrew and Greek Lexicon Study Index
usageNote: This index supplies lookup keys and study prompts only. Always retrieve the full lemma, senses, transliteration and morphology from the linked lexicon/interlinear source. A Strong's number is an index, not a complete definition. Meanings vary by context; do not assign a lemma to an English word unless the verse-level source alignment verifies it.

entries.studyLabel: The divine name
entries.contextPrompt: Study how the name is revealed in its narrative and covenant setting. Respect the distinction between the Hebrew name and English translation conventions.

entries.studyLabel: God; gods; divine beings, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: The form and meaning must be interpreted from syntax and context; do not assume the same English rendering in every occurrence.

entries.studyLabel: Steadfast love; covenant loyalty; kindness, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Explore the relational and covenant setting. No single English gloss captures every use.

entries.studyLabel: Peace; well-being; wholeness, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Read whether the passage concerns greeting, safety, communal well-being, reconciliation or peace.

entries.studyLabel: Faithfulness; firmness; trustworthiness, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Compare the passage's emphasis on reliability, faithful conduct or trust; avoid forcing one English gloss.

entries.studyLabel: Truth; reliability; faithfulness, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Observe whether the word describes truthful speech, dependable character or covenant reliability.

entries.studyLabel: Wind; breath; spirit, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: The word has a broad semantic range. Determine from grammar and context whether wind, breath or spirit is intended.

entries.studyLabel: Knowledge; understanding, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Study the relationship between knowledge, covenant faithfulness and wise action in the surrounding passage.

entries.studyLabel: Word; message; account, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Do not assume every occurrence refers to Jesus as a title; examine syntax and literary context.

entries.studyLabel: Love; care or regard, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Study the action and object of love in context. Avoid simplistic claims that one Greek word always means a uniquely higher kind of love.

entries.studyLabel: Faith; trust; faithfulness, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Examine whether the passage emphasises trust, belief, faithfulness or a related sense.

entries.studyLabel: Grace; favour; gracious gift, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Track how grace functions in the argument; distinguish divine favour from the effects it produces.

entries.studyLabel: Salvation; deliverance, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Determine whether the passage concerns rescue, present deliverance or final salvation.

entries.studyLabel: Spirit; wind; breath, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Use grammar and context to identify whether the passage refers to the Holy Spirit, human spirit, or wind/breath.

entries.studyLabel: Righteousness; justice, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Compare ethical, covenantal and saving dimensions in context; do not flatten the term into one English phrase.

entries.studyLabel: Eternal; belonging to an age, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Consider the phrase and its contrast in context; avoid building a complete doctrine from an isolated gloss.

entries.studyLabel: Repentance; change of mind and direction
entries.contextPrompt: Read repentance with the call to turn toward God and its observable fruit; avoid reducing it to regret alone.

entries.studyLabel: Covenant; treaty, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Study the parties, promises, obligations and signs in the specific covenant passage.

entries.studyLabel: Righteousness; justice, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Observe whether the context concerns right conduct, just judgment or the character of a righteous ruler.

entries.studyLabel: Instruction; teaching; law, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: The term can refer broadly to instruction or specifically to law; read the literary and covenant setting.

entries.studyLabel: Word; matter; thing, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Check whether the word refers to spoken message, event, matter or thing in the passage.

entries.studyLabel: Beginning; first; chief, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Examine its grammatical role and phrase; do not infer a complete doctrine from the gloss alone.

entries.studyLabel: Peace; harmony; well-being, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Consider whether the context describes peace with God, communal harmony, greeting or well-being.

entries.studyLabel: Holy; set apart, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Observe whether the term describes God, the Spirit, a person or something consecrated.

entries.studyLabel: Mercy; compassion, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Read the need, recipient and action of mercy in context; distinguish mercy from a merely sentimental feeling.

entries.studyLabel: Glory; honour; reputation, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Determine whether the passage speaks of divine splendour, honour, reputation or praise.

entries.studyLabel: Assembly; congregation; church, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Study the local assembly and wider people of God in context; avoid reducing the word to a modern building.

entries.studyLabel: Good news; gospel message
entries.contextPrompt: Identify the content of the good news in the author's argument and its connection to Jesus.

entries.studyLabel: Remain; abide; stay, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Trace what or whom the subject remains in, and how the passage describes the result of abiding.

entries.studyLabel: To love; show love, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Study the subject, object and action of love; do not claim the verb always carries one fixed technical meaning.

entries.studyLabel: Son; descendant, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Distinguish literal, genealogical, royal and relational uses from the surrounding passage.

entries.studyLabel: Encouragement; exhortation; consolation, according to context
entries.contextPrompt: Check whether the context emphasises comfort, encouragement, appeal or exhortation.
